# Semantic Project Indexing Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** Enable `tp index [path]` to semantically index a project's directory tree via AI, and integrate semantic search into the navigation cascade so queries like `tp webhook handler` match by meaning.

**Architecture:** New `project_dirs` SQLite table stores per-directory descriptions generated by a single Claude Haiku API call. At query time, local keyword matching against descriptions is tried first; if ambiguous, an AI fallback picks the best match. Integrates as step 5.5 in the existing navigation cascade.

**Tech Stack:** Rust, rusqlite, reqwest (behind `ai` feature flag), serde_json, Anthropic Messages API

```rust
use anyhow::Result;
use rusqlite::Connection;

/// Directories to always skip when walking a project tree.
const IGNORED_DIRS: &[&str] = &[
    ".git",
    "node_modules",
    "target",
    "__pycache__",
    ".venv",
    "dist",
    "build",
    ".next",
    ".cache",
    "vendor",
    ".idea",
    ".vscode",
    ".DS_Store",
    "venv",
    ".tox",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".pytest_cache",
    "coverage",
    ".turbo",
];

/// Maximum directory depth to scan.
const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 3;

/// Parse a `.gitignore` file and extract simple directory-name patterns.
///
/// Only handles plain names and `name/` patterns — globs with `*` or `**`
/// and negations (`!`) are skipped. This is a pragmatic 80/20 approach.
fn parse_gitignore(content: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    content
        .lines()
        .map(|l| l.trim())
        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#') && !l.starts_with('!'))
        .filter(|l| !l.contains('*'))
        .map(|l| l.trim_start_matches('/').trim_end_matches('/').to_string())
        .filter(|l| !l.contains('/') && !l.is_empty())
        .collect()
}

/// Walk a project directory tree up to MAX_DEPTH levels, skipping ignored dirs.
/// Returns a sorted list of relative directory paths (e.g. "src/ai", "docs/book").
fn walk_tree(root: &std::path::Path, extra_ignores: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut dirs = Vec::new();
    walk_recursive(root, root, 0, extra_ignores, &mut dirs);
    dirs.sort();
    dirs
}

fn walk_recursive(
    base: &std::path::Path,
    current: &std::path::Path,
    depth: usize,
    extra_ignores: &[String],
    result: &mut Vec<String>,
) {
    if depth >= MAX_DEPTH {
        return;
    }

    let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(current) {
        Ok(e) => e,
        Err(_) => return,
    };

    for entry in entries.flatten() {
        let path = entry.path();
        if !path.is_dir() {
            continue;
        }

        let name = match entry.file_name().to_str() {
            Some(n) => n.to_string(),
            None => continue,
        };

        // Skip if in hardcoded ignore list
        if IGNORED_DIRS.contains(&name.as_str()) {
            continue;
        }

        // Skip if in gitignore-derived list
        if extra_ignores.iter().any(|ig| ig == &name) {
            continue;
        }

        // Build relative path
        if let Ok(rel) = path.strip_prefix(base) {
            result.push(rel.to_string_lossy().to_string());
        }

        walk_recursive(base, &path, depth + 1, extra_ignores, result);
    }
}

/// Build the prompt to send to the AI for indexing.
fn build_index_prompt(project_name: &str, project_kind: Option<&str>, dirs: &[String]) -> String {
    let mut prompt = String::new();
    prompt.push_str(&format!(
        "Project: {} ({})\nDirectories:\n",
        project_name,
        project_kind.unwrap_or("unknown")
    ));
    for dir in dirs {
        prompt.push_str(&format!("  {}/\n", dir));
    }
    prompt.push_str(
        "\nFor each directory, write a short (5-15 word) description of what it likely contains \
         based on its name, position in the tree, and the project type.\n\
         Return ONLY valid JSON: {\"dir_path\": \"description\", ...}\n\
         Do not include markdown formatting or code fences.",
    );
    prompt
}

/// Parse the AI response JSON into a map of rel_path -> description.
fn parse_index_response(text: &str) -> Option<std::collections::HashMap<String, String>> {
    // Strip markdown code fences if the model wraps the response
    let cleaned = text
        .trim()
        .strip_prefix("```json")
        .or_else(|| text.trim().strip_prefix("```"))
        .unwrap_or(text.trim());
    let cleaned = cleaned.strip_suffix("```").unwrap_or(cleaned).trim();

    serde_json::from_str(cleaned).ok()
}

/// Save index results to the database, replacing any previous index for this project.
fn save_index(
    conn: &Connection,
    project_root: &str,
    entries: &std::collections::HashMap<String, String>,
) -> Result<()> {
    // Clear previous entries for this project
    conn.execute(
        "DELETE FROM project_dirs WHERE project_root = ?1",
        [project_root],
    )?;

    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(
        "INSERT INTO project_dirs (project_root, rel_path, description) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)",
    )?;

    for (rel_path, description) in entries {
        // Normalize: strip trailing slash if present
        let path = rel_path.trim_end_matches('/');
        stmt.execute(rusqlite::params![project_root, path, description])?;
    }

    // Update the projects table indexed_at timestamp
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO projects (path, name, kind, indexed_at)
         VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, strftime('%s','now'))
         ON CONFLICT(path) DO UPDATE SET indexed_at = strftime('%s','now')",
        rusqlite::params![
            project_root,
            crate::project::project_name(project_root),
            crate::project::project_kind(project_root).unwrap_or("unknown"),
        ],
    )?;

    Ok(())
}

/// Run semantic indexing on a project. This is the main entry point called
/// by the CLI `tp index [path]` command.
///
/// 1. Detects the project root from the given path
/// 2. Walks the directory tree (top 3 levels, filtered)
/// 3. Sends one API call to Claude Haiku for descriptions
/// 4. Stores results in the `project_dirs` table
#[cfg(feature = "ai")]
pub fn index_project(conn: &Connection, target: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let abs = std::fs::canonicalize(target)
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| std::path::PathBuf::from(target));

    let project_root = crate::project::detect_project_root(abs.to_str().unwrap_or(target))
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(
            "No project root found at {}. Look for .git, Cargo.toml, package.json, etc.",
            abs.display()
        ))?;

    let root_path = std::path::Path::new(&project_root);
    let name = crate::project::project_name(&project_root);
    let kind = crate::project::project_kind(&project_root);

    eprintln!("Indexing project: {} ({})", name, kind.unwrap_or("unknown"));

    // Parse .gitignore for extra ignores
    let gitignore_path = root_path.join(".gitignore");
    let extra_ignores = if gitignore_path.exists() {
        std::fs::read_to_string(&gitignore_path)
            .map(|content| parse_gitignore(&content))
            .unwrap_or_default()
    } else {
        Vec::new()
    };

    // Walk the tree
    let dirs = walk_tree(root_path, &extra_ignores);

    if dirs.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("No directories found to index.");
        return Ok(());
    }

    eprintln!("Found {} directories", dirs.len());

    // Check for API key
    let (api_key, _source) = super::detect_api_key()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("No API key found. Run: tp --setup-ai"))?;

    // Build prompt and call AI
    let prompt = build_index_prompt(&name, kind, &dirs);

    let model =
        std::env::var("TP_AI_MODEL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001".to_string());

    let timeout_ms: u64 = std::env::var("TP_AI_TIMEOUT")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(10_000); // 10s default for indexing (more generous than reranking)

    let body = serde_json::json!({
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "system": "You are a code project analyzer. Given a project's directory tree, describe what each directory likely contains. Return ONLY valid JSON mapping directory paths to short descriptions. No markdown, no code fences, no explanation.",
        "messages": [
            { "role": "user", "content": prompt }
        ]
    });

    let spinner = crate::style::Spinner::start("indexing project...");

    let client = reqwest::blocking::Client::builder()
        .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_millis(timeout_ms))
        .build()?;

    let resp = client
        .post("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages")
        .header("x-api-key", &api_key)
        .header("anthropic-version", "2023-06-01")
        .header("content-type", "application/json")
        .json(&body)
        .send()?;

    spinner.stop();

    if !resp.status().is_success() {
        let status = resp.status();
        let body_text = resp.text().unwrap_or_default();
        anyhow::bail!("API returned status {}: {}", status, body_text);
    }

    let json: serde_json::Value = resp.json()?;
    let text = json["content"][0]["text"]
        .as_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Unexpected API response format"))?;

    let entries = parse_index_response(text)
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Failed to parse AI response as JSON: {}", text))?;

    // Save to database
    save_index(conn, &project_root, &entries)?;

    eprintln!("Indexed {} directories for {}", entries.len(), name);

    // Show a sample
    let mut sample: Vec<_> = entries.iter().collect();
    sample.sort_by_key(|(k, _)| k.clone());
    for (path, desc) in sample.iter().take(5) {
        eprintln!("  {}: {}", path, desc);
    }
    if entries.len() > 5 {
        eprintln!("  ... and {} more", entries.len() - 5);
    }

    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(not(feature = "ai"))]
pub fn index_project(_conn: &Connection, _target: &str) -> Result<()> {
    eprintln!("AI features are not enabled. Rebuild with --features ai");
    Ok(())
}

**Step 1: Write the module with tests**

Create `src/ai/semantic.rs`:

```rust
use anyhow::Result;
use rusqlite::Connection;

/// A semantic search result — a directory that matched by description.
pub struct SemanticMatch {
    pub path: String,
    pub rel_path: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub keyword_score: usize,
}

/// Search the semantic index for directories matching the query terms.
///
/// Performs case-insensitive keyword matching against stored descriptions.
/// Returns matches sorted by number of terms matched (descending).
pub fn keyword_search(
    conn: &Connection,
    project_root: &str,
    query_terms: &[&str],
) -> Result<Vec<SemanticMatch>> {
    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(
        "SELECT rel_path, description FROM project_dirs WHERE project_root = ?1",
    )?;

    let rows = stmt.query_map([project_root], |row| {
        Ok((row.get::<_, String>(0)?, row.get::<_, String>(1)?))
    })?;

    let mut matches: Vec<SemanticMatch> = Vec::new();

    for row in rows {
        let (rel_path, description) = row?;
        let desc_lower = description.to_lowercase();

        // Count how many query terms appear in the description
        let score = query_terms
            .iter()
            .filter(|term| desc_lower.contains(&term.to_lowercase()))
            .count();

        if score > 0 {
            let full_path = format!("{}/{}", project_root.trim_end_matches('/'), rel_path);
            matches.push(SemanticMatch {
                path: full_path,
                rel_path,
                description,
                keyword_score: score,
            });
        }
    }

    // Sort by score descending, then by path length ascending (prefer shallower)
    matches.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b.keyword_score
            .cmp(&a.keyword_score)
            .then_with(|| a.rel_path.len().cmp(&b.rel_path.len()))
    });

    Ok(matches)
}

/// Use AI to pick the best semantic match when keyword matching is ambiguous.
///
/// Sends the query and candidate descriptions to Claude Haiku, asks it to
/// pick the best match. Returns the full path of the chosen directory,
/// or None if AI is unavailable or fails.
#[cfg(feature = "ai")]
pub fn ai_semantic_search(
    query: &str,
    matches: &[SemanticMatch],
) -> Option<String> {
    if matches.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }

    let (api_key, _) = super::detect_api_key()?;

    let mut prompt = format!("Query: {}\n\nIndexed directories:\n", query);
    for (i, m) in matches.iter().enumerate().take(10) {
        prompt.push_str(&format!("  {}: {} — {}\n", i, m.rel_path, m.description));
    }
    prompt.push_str("\nReturn ONLY the 0-based index of the directory that best matches the query. No explanation.");

    let model =
        std::env::var("TP_AI_MODEL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001".to_string());

    let timeout_ms: u64 = std::env::var("TP_AI_TIMEOUT")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(2000);

    let body = serde_json::json!({
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": 50,
        "system": "You are a directory navigation assistant. Given a natural language query and indexed directory descriptions, pick the single best match.",
        "messages": [
            { "role": "user", "content": prompt }
        ]
    });

    let spinner = crate::style::Spinner::start("searching index...");

    let result = (|| -> Option<String> {
        let client = reqwest::blocking::Client::builder()
            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_millis(timeout_ms))
            .build()
            .ok()?;

        let resp = client
            .post("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages")
            .header("x-api-key", &api_key)
            .header("anthropic-version", "2023-06-01")
            .header("content-type", "application/json")
            .json(&body)
            .send()
            .ok()?;

        let json: serde_json::Value = resp.json().ok()?;
        let text = json["content"][0]["text"].as_str()?;
        let index: usize = text.trim().parse().ok()?;

        matches.get(index).map(|m| m.path.clone())
    })();

    spinner.stop();
    result
}

#[cfg(not(feature = "ai"))]
pub fn ai_semantic_search(
    _query: &str,
    _matches: &[SemanticMatch],
) -> Option<String> {
    None
}

/// Check if a project's semantic index is stale (older than 30 days).
/// Returns the project name if stale, None otherwise.
pub fn check_staleness(conn: &Connection, project_root: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let row = conn
        .query_row(
            "SELECT name, indexed_at FROM projects WHERE path = ?1 AND indexed_at IS NOT NULL",
            [project_root],
            |row| Ok((row.get::<_, String>(0)?, row.get::<_, i64>(1)?)),
        )
        .ok()?;

    let (name, indexed_at) = row;
    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .ok()?
        .as_secs() as i64;

    let thirty_days = 30 * 24 * 3600;
    if now - indexed_at > thirty_days {
        Some(name)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// Check if a project has a semantic index at all.
pub fn has_index(conn: &Connection, project_root: &str) -> bool {
    conn.query_row(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM project_dirs WHERE project_root = ?1",
        [project_root],
        |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0),
    )
    .unwrap_or(0)
        > 0
}

        .unwrap();
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO project_dirs (project_root, rel_path, description) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)",
            ["/projects/myapp", "tests", "Test suites and fixtures"],
        )
        .unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_keyword_search_single_term() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        setup_indexed_project(&conn);

        let results = keyword_search(&conn, "/projects/myapp", &["webhook"]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(results.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(results[0].rel_path, "src/webhooks");
        assert_eq!(results[0].keyword_score, 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_keyword_search_multiple_terms() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        setup_indexed_project(&conn);

        let results = keyword_search(&conn, "/projects/myapp", &["webhook", "retry"]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(results.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(results[0].keyword_score, 2); // both terms match
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_keyword_search_no_match() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        setup_indexed_project(&conn);

        let results = keyword_search(&conn, "/projects/myapp", &["database"]).unwrap();
        assert!(results.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_keyword_search_case_insensitive() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        setup_indexed_project(&conn);

        let results = keyword_search(&conn, "/projects/myapp", &["API"]).unwrap();
        assert!(!results.is_empty());
        assert!(results.iter().any(|r| r.rel_path == "src/api"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_keyword_search_ranked_by_score() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        setup_indexed_project(&conn);

        // "auth" matches both "auth" and "authorization" in the auth module,
        // but "middleware" only matches auth. Let's search for terms that
        // produce different scores.
        let results = keyword_search(&conn, "/projects/myapp", &["handling", "retry"]).unwrap();
        // "src/webhooks" has both "handling" and "retry" in its description
        assert!(!results.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(results[0].rel_path, "src/webhooks");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_keyword_search_builds_full_path() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        setup_indexed_project(&conn);

        let results = keyword_search(&conn, "/projects/myapp", &["webhook"]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(results[0].path, "/projects/myapp/src/webhooks");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_has_index_true() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        setup_indexed_project(&conn);

        assert!(has_index(&conn, "/projects/myapp"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_has_index_false() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        assert!(!has_index(&conn, "/projects/nothing"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_check_staleness_no_project() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        assert!(check_staleness(&conn, "/nonexistent").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_check_staleness_fresh() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO projects (path, name, kind, indexed_at) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, strftime('%s','now'))",
            ["/projects/myapp", "myapp", "rust"],
        )
        .unwrap();

        // Just indexed — should not be stale
        assert!(check_staleness(&conn, "/projects/myapp").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_check_staleness_old() {
        let conn = db::open_memory().unwrap();
        // 31 days ago
        let old_timestamp = std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .unwrap()
            .as_secs() as i64
            - (31 * 24 * 3600);

        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO projects (path, name, kind, indexed_at) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4)",
            rusqlite::params!["/projects/myapp", "myapp", "rust", old_timestamp],
        )
        .unwrap();

        let result = check_staleness(&conn, "/projects/myapp");
        assert_eq!(result, Some("myapp".to_string()));
    }
}

**Step 1: Update ai-features.md**

Move the "Semantic Project Indexing" section from "Coming Soon (Stubbed)" to "Implemented Features", after "Session Recall". Add usage details:

```markdown
### Semantic Project Indexing

Index a project's directory tree by concept, enabling natural language searches:

```sh
tp index            # index the current project
tp index /path/to   # index a specific project
```

Once indexed, queries match against directory descriptions:

```sh
tp webhook handler   # finds src/webhooks/ even without "webhook" in the path
tp auth middleware   # finds src/auth/ based on its semantic description
```

**How it works:**
1. Walks the directory tree (top 3 levels, skipping noise like `node_modules`, `.git`, etc.)
2. Sends the tree structure to Claude Haiku in a single API call
3. Stores per-directory descriptions in SQLite
4. At query time, matches against descriptions with local keyword search first, falling back to AI only when ambiguous

The index respects `.gitignore` patterns. If an index is older than 30 days, `tp` will nudge you to re-index.
```
